exposure: infant size for gestational age (small for gestational age, large for gestational age, normal)
cohort: 1,261,948 singleton infants born at term (gestational age ≥37 weeks) in Sweden between 1999 and 2012
finding: Several maternal and obstetric factors were identified as risk factors for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, including gestational age 37 to 38 weeks, failed vacuum extraction, vacuum extraction, Asian mother, primipara, large-for-gestational-age infant, obese mother, and small-for-gestational-age infant, while planned cesarean delivery was associated with a reduced risk.
mod_finding: Vacuum extraction and failed vacuum extraction were associated with an increased risk of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, while planned cesarean delivery was associated with a reduced risk.
